### Symbols for probability and statistics

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $(\Omega, \mathcal F, \mathbb P)$ | probability space: sample space $\Omega$, $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal F$, probability measure $\mathbb P$ |
| $\mathbb P(A)$, $\mathbb P(A \mid B)$ | probability of an event, conditional probability |
| $X$, $Y$, $Z$ | random variables (uppercase); their values $x$, $y$, $z$ |
| $\mathbf x$ | random vector (bold lowercase), with its law stated |
| $p(x)$, $p_X(x)$ | density or mass function (of $X$) |
| $p(x \mid y)$, $p_{X,Y}(x, y)$ | conditional and joint density or mass function |
| $x \sim p$ | $x$ is drawn from the distribution $p$ |
| $\mathbb E[X]$, $\mathbb E_{x\sim p}[\cdot]$ | expectation (under $p$) |
| $\mathbb E[X \mid Y]$ | conditional expectation |
| $\operatorname{Var}(X)$ | variance |
| $\operatorname{Cov}(X, Y)$ | covariance |
| $\mu$, $\sigma^2$, $\sigma$ | mean, variance, standard deviation |
| $\boldsymbol\mu$ | mean vector |
| $\Sigma$ | covariance matrix (plain, an exception to bold matrices) |
| $\mathcal N(\mu, \sigma^2)$, $\mathcal N(\boldsymbol\mu, \Sigma)$ | normal (Gaussian) distribution |
| $\mathcal N(\mathbf x \mid \boldsymbol\mu, \Sigma)$ | its density at $\mathbf x$ |
| $\operatorname{Bern}(p)$, $\operatorname{Bin}(n, p)$ | Bernoulli and binomial distributions with success probability $p$ |
| $\bar X_n$ | sample mean of $X_1, \dots, X_n$ |
| $\hat\theta$ | estimator of a parameter $\theta$ |
| $H(X)$, $H(X \mid Y)$ | entropy (differential entropy when $X$ is continuous), conditional entropy |
| $H(p, q)$ | cross-entropy |
| $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p \,\Vert\, q)$ | Kullback-Leibler divergence |
| $I(X; Y)$ | mutual information |
| $\langle A\rangle = \langle\psi, A\psi\rangle$ | quantum expectation value in the state $\psi$ |
| $\langle\cdot\rangle_\beta$ | thermal average at inverse temperature $\beta$ |

Conventions:

- $\mathbb E$ is the expectation of a random variable; $\langle\cdot\rangle$ is a quantum or thermal average.
- $\mathbb P$ is a probability; $p$ is a density or mass function.
- Entropy, cross-entropy, Kullback-Leibler divergence and mutual information use the natural logarithm (nats).
